title: GraphRAG
hook: GraphRAG builds a knowledge graph from your documents first, then answers over its structure — so it can reason across many sources, not just retrieve the nearest few chunks.
key_points: Microsoft Research technique (2024) that combines knowledge graphs with RAG.
Extracts entities and relationships into a graph, then summarizes graph 'communities'.
Answers global, multi-hop questions that flat vector retrieval handles poorly.
Trades extra indexing cost for better synthesis across a whole corpus.
content_html: GraphRAG, introduced by Microsoft Research in 2024, addresses a weakness of ordinary retrieval-augmented generation: vector search finds the chunks most similar to a query, but struggles with questions that require connecting information spread across many documents. GraphRAG instead builds a knowledge graph from the corpus up front and uses that structure to answer.
extra_html:
How it works

In an indexing phase, an LLM extracts entities and the relationships between them from the raw text, assembling a knowledge graph. It then detects "communities" of densely connected entities and generates summaries for each, building a hierarchy from local clusters up to the whole corpus. At query time, GraphRAG can draw on these community summaries to answer broad, global questions ("what are the main themes?") as well as drill into specific multi-hop ones — tasks where retrieving a handful of nearby chunks falls short.

Why it matters

GraphRAG shows that the retrieval half of RAG is itself a rich design space: how you structure and index knowledge shapes which questions the system can answer. The cost is heavier, LLM-driven indexing, but for narrative or analytical queries over private data, reasoning over an explicit graph beats nearest-neighbor lookup — a key pattern as RAG matured beyond simple vector search.

related.title: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data
related.hook: An LLM only knows what it was trained on — until it's stale, private, or just wrong. RAG bolts on a search step so the model answers from your data and can cite it.

related.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
related.hook: Why force a model to memorize everything? RAG lets it look things up — fetch relevant documents, then answer from that evidence instead of frozen weights alone.

related.title: Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR)
related.hook: Keyword search misses answers that use different words. DPR embeds questions and passages into one vector space and retrieves by meaning — the backbone of modern vector search.

flashcards.explanation_html: GraphRAG builds a knowledge graph, detects densely-connected communities, and generates hierarchical summaries for them.

flashcards.prompt: What tradeoff does GraphRAG make for better cross-corpus synthesis?
flashcards.back_html: It pays a heavier, LLM-driven indexing cost up front in exchange for answering global, multi-hop questions that flat vector retrieval handles poorly.
